title: 喜见外弟又言别
title_en: Glad to Meet My Cousin, Then Saying Goodbye Again
author: 李益

readings.zh: “几重”是几层，“重”读 chóng，不读 zhòng。
readings.en: Here it means layers, so it is read chóng, not zhòng.

glosses.zh: 离乱：因为战乱，家人离散。这里指安史之乱以后多年的动乱。
glosses.en: lí luàn: families torn apart by war. Here, the years of fighting after the An Lushan Rebellion.

glosses.zh: 一相逢：一下子遇见了，终于见了一面。
glosses.en: yī xiāng féng: suddenly meeting, at last seeing each other.
wèn xìng: asking what his family name is.

glosses.zh: 惊初见：吃惊地以为是第一次见面的陌生人。
glosses.en: jīng chū jiàn: surprised, thinking this is a stranger met for the first time.
chēng míng: he says his given name.
jiù róng: how he looked long ago, as a child.

glosses.zh: 沧海事：“沧海桑田”的意思，大海变成桑田，比喻世事变化很大。
glosses.en: cāng hǎi shì: from the saying that the blue sea turns into mulberry fields; it means the world has changed enormously.
yǔ bà: when the talking is over.

glosses.zh: 暮天钟：傍晚寺庙里敲响的钟声。
glosses.en: mù tiān zhōng: the temple bell that rings at dusk.

glosses.zh: 巴陵：地名，在今天湖南岳阳。
glosses.en: bā líng: a place, today's Yueyang in Hunan.
jǐ chóng: how many layers, how many ranges.

translation.zh: 经过十年的战乱和离散，
translation.en: After ten years of war and scattering,

translation.zh: 我们都长大了，才终于见面。
translation.en: we have grown up, and at last we meet.

translation.zh: 问起姓氏，我吃惊地以为是初次见面的人；
translation.en: When I ask his family name, I am surprised, as if meeting a stranger;

translation.zh: 等他说出名字，我才想起他小时候的样子。
translation.en: when he tells me his name, I remember the face he had as a child.

translation.zh: 我们说起分别以来天翻地覆的变化，
translation.en: We talk about the huge changes since we parted,

translation.zh: 说完时，傍晚寺庙的钟声已经响了。
translation.en: and when we finish, the evening temple bell is ringing.

translation.zh: 明天你就要走上去巴陵的路，
translation.en: Tomorrow you set off on the road to Baling,

translation.zh: 中间又要隔着几重秋天的山啊。
translation.en: and how many autumn mountains will lie between us again?

background.zh: 李益小时候经历了安史之乱，之后好多年天下不太平，亲人四处离散。这首诗写他和表弟分别十年后偶然重逢。“外弟”是表弟，就是姑妈或舅舅家的弟弟。两人一起说了很久的话，第二天表弟又要往巴陵去了，所以题目说“喜见”又“言别”。具体写于哪一年不详。
background.en: Li Yi lived through the An Lushan Rebellion as a child, and for many years afterward the land was unsettled and families were scattered. This poem is about meeting his younger cousin by chance after ten years apart. They talked for a long time, but the next day the cousin had to leave for Baling. So the title says he was glad to see him, and then had to say goodbye. The exact year is not known.

author_note.zh: 李益（约746—约829），唐代诗人，年轻时考中进士，曾经长期在北方边塞的军队里做事。他最擅长写七言绝句，边塞诗很有名，比如《夜上受降城闻笛》。这首五言律诗写的是亲人之间的离合，语言朴素，感情真切。
author_note.en: Li Yi (about 746 to about 829) was a Tang poet. He passed the highest exam when young and spent many years working in armies on the northern frontier. He was best at seven-character quatrains, and his frontier poems are famous, such as "Hearing a Flute on the Wall of Shouxiang at Night". This poem is about family members meeting and parting, in plain words with true feeling.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗最妙的是中间“问姓惊初见，称名忆旧容”两句。分别时都是孩子，再见时已经长大，面对面也认不出来，只好先问姓什么。一听名字，才猛然想起小时候的模样。一“惊”一“忆”，把重逢那一刻又意外又惊喜的样子写活了。接着两人说了很久，说到天黑钟响，十年的变化一夜说不完。可是高兴还没过去，明天又要分别，前面是一层又一层的秋山。整首诗从喜到悲，短短四十个字，写尽了乱世里亲人聚少离多的无奈。
appreciation.en: The best part is the middle pair of lines. They parted as children and meet again as grown-ups. Face to face, they do not know each other, so he first asks the family name. Hearing the given name, he suddenly remembers the child's face. One word for surprise and one for remembering bring that moment of shock and joy to life. Then they talk until the evening bell rings; ten years of change cannot be told in one night. But the joy is not over before parting comes again, with layer after layer of autumn mountains ahead. In just forty characters the poem moves from joy to sorrow, and shows how in times of war, families meet rarely and part often.
